title: World Development Indicators: consumer-price inflation of the G7 and Switzerland 1965-1990; the export shares of fuel, food and agricultural raw materials and the manufacturing share of GDP of Nigeria, the Netherlands, Norway and the United Kingdom 1960-1990; total natural-resource rents of every economy in 1970 and 1990
source: World Bank, World Development Indicators (source 2 of the API v2, lastupdated 2026-11-11)
series: indicator, countrycode, country, year, value: the observations of the API that are not empty and not of an aggregate (an economy whose region is 'NA' in the API's list of countries); the rents in 1970 and 1990 only. The indicators, in the API's words: FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG ('Inflation, consumer prices (annual %)'); TX.VAL.FUEL.ZS.UN ('Fuel exports (% of merchandise exports)'); TX.VAL.FOOD.ZS.UN ('Food exports (% of merchandise exports)'); TX.VAL.AGRI.ZS.UN ('Agricultural raw materials exports (% of merchandise exports)'); NV.IND.MANF.ZS ('Manufacturing, value added (% of GDP)'); NY.GDP.TOTL.RT.ZS ('Total natural resources rents (% of GDP)'). The definition of the rents is quoted in oil_facts (row wdi_rents_def).
license: CC BY 4.0. The World Bank's page of the Pink Sheet (https://www.worldbank.org/en/research/commodity-markets, read on 2026-11-27) lists under 'Using this Data': 'Summary terms of use' (https://data.worldbank.org/summary-terms-of-use), 'Terms of use for Datasets' (https://www.worldbank.org/en/about/legal/terms-of-use-for-datasets) and 'Data Access and Licensing' (https://datacatalog.worldbank.org/public-licenses#cc-by). That page says: 'The World Bank Group makes data publicly available according to open data standards and licenses datasets under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International license (CC-BY 4.0).' and 'Users are only obligated to give appropriate credit (attribution) and indicate if they have made any changes, including translations.' (rows ps_using, wb_cc and wb_attr of oil_facts). The metadata of NY.GDP.TOTL.RT.ZS give 'License_Type CC BY-4.0 License_URL https://datacatalog.worldbank.org/public-licenses#cc-by' (row wdi_license of oil_facts). The book credits the World Bank's World Development Indicators under each figure and in the bibliography (wdi47) and says that the regressions and the means are its own calculation.
citation: World Bank, World Development Indicators, API v2, lastupdated 2026-11-11 (bibitem wdi47 of Chapter 47)
notes: The API returns the series of the whole period in one page (per_page=20000; data/fetch/oil47.py checks 'pages' = 1). A value is stored as the API gives it (repr of the float). The aggregates are recognised by the API's own list of countries (wdicountries_47), not by a list of the book's.
